batches.title: Green Lentils (Mon–Thu lunches)
steps: Rinse 300 g dried green lentils in cold water.
Place in a medium saucepan, cover with at least 5 cm of cold water.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered 20–22 min until tender but holding their shape.
Drain in a colander, rinse briefly with cold water to stop cooking.
Season lightly with salt. Cool completely before storing.
Transfer to an airtight container. Label: 'Lentils — cooked Sunday 20/09. Use by Friday 25/09.'

day_of_assembly.Monday: Lunch — Mediterranean Beef & Lentil Bowl: reheat 150g (Diego) / 120g (Diana) lentils in a pan with 1 tsp red wine vinegar, cumin and black pepper 3 min; combine with reheated beef mince and aubergine over quinoa.
day_of_assembly.Thursday: Lunch — French Lentil & Roasted Carrot Bowl: reheat 150g (Diego) / 120g (Diana) lentils in a pan with 1 tsp olive oil and red wine vinegar 3 min; serve over roasted carrots with a boiled egg and sourdough croutons.

storage.safety_note: Cooked beans and lentils keep well. Freeze in portions for quick meals.

batches.title: Sweet Potato Mash (Mon–Tue dinners)
steps: Peel 800 g sweet potatoes and cut into 3 cm cubes.
Place in a large saucepan, cover with cold salted water.
Bring to a boil and cook 18–20 min until very tender when pierced with a fork.
Drain well; return to the warm pot for 1 min to steam-dry.
Mash thoroughly with 1 tsp olive oil and a good pinch of black pepper until smooth.
Cool completely. Transfer to an airtight container.
Label: 'Sweet potato mash — cooked Sunday. Use Mon (day 1) and Tue (day 2) only.'

day_of_assembly.Monday: Dinner — Soy-Ginger Baked Salmon with Spinach: microwave 200g (Diego) / 150g (Diana) mash 2 min; serve as base for baked salmon fillet and stir-fried spinach.
day_of_assembly.Tuesday: Dinner — Asian Tilapia with Stir-Fried Courgette & Mushrooms: microwave 180g (Diego) / 140g (Diana) mash 2 min; plate as base under pan-seared tilapia with sesame-ginger stir-fried courgette and mushrooms.

storage.safety_note: Cooked vegetables store well. Roasted veg can be eaten cold in salads.
